metadata.title: Pakistan Flood Data (2010-2026)
metadata.description: Comprehensive flood impact data for Pakistan including deaths, affected populations, and district-level information
metadata.disclaimer: Figures are approximate and based on publicly available reports. Exact numbers may vary by source and reporting period.

yearlySummary.description: One of the worst humanitarian disasters in Pakistan's history. 1/5th of country submerged. Described as a 'tsunami in slow motion'.
Massive monsoon rains devastated Sindh province. 16 districts affected with record-breaking rainfall 8-10x drainage capacity.
Third consecutive year of major flooding. Severe impacts in Sindh, southern Punjab, and Balochistan.
Flash floods affected parts of Punjab, KP, Sindh, and Balochistan. Multiple provinces hit simultaneously.
Severe riverine and flash flooding, especially along the Chenab and Jhelum rivers. Punjab and AJK worst affected.
Monsoon rains combined with GLOF (Glacial Lake Outburst Flood) events. KP and Chitral regions severely hit.
Pre-monsoon and monsoon rains caused flash floods. 56% of fatalities occurred in KP. Karakoram Highway blocked.
Localized monsoon impacts. Riverine and low-lying districts primarily affected.
Typical seasonal flooding with manageable impacts compared to mega-flood years.
Widespread flooding and landslides, particularly in KP, Balochistan, and AJK. Mardan and Dir Lower worst hit.
Record-breaking monsoon rainfall. Sindh declared calamity-affected. Karachi received heaviest rainfall in 89 years (490mm in August).
Less catastrophic than surrounding years but still resulted in significant rain-related fatalities across multiple provinces.
The 'Monsoon on Steroids'. Nearly 1/3 of country submerged. 84 districts declared calamity-hit. Worst disaster since 2010.
Recovery year post-2022. Localized flash floods. Sutlej River belt badly hit, causing displacement of nearly 1 million.
Significantly above-average monsoon rainfall. 13 districts in Balochistan declared calamity-hit. Heavy impact in Sindh and Punjab.
Devastating monsoon floods from June-September. Worst riverine flooding in decades in Punjab. 2.5M acres farmland damaged.
Ongoing monsoon season as of September 2026. Urban flooding in Rawalpindi/Islamabad. Flash floods and landslide risks in northern regions.
